attribution: Framed as the teaching of the sage Gheranda to his student Chanda Kapali; actual author unknown
period: Generally placed in the late 17th or 18th century CE; dating is uncertain
summary: A late hatha yoga manual that organises practice into seven limbs, from bodily purification to samadhi.
whyRead: It is one of the most systematic hatha manuals, with detailed lists of cleansing practices, postures and seals. Comparing its seven limbs with Patanjali's eight shows how yoga was reshaped over time.
story: The text is framed as a dialogue in which the sage Gheranda teaches Chanda Kapali, who asks about the yoga of the body (ghata, the "vessel").
questions: What does it mean to treat the body as a vessel to be purified?
How does a sevenfold yoga differ from the eightfold scheme?

keyTeachings.title: The body as a vessel
keyTeachings.text: The text calls its discipline ghatastha yoga, yoga of the "vessel". The body is to be refined like unfired clay, so that it can hold the higher stages of practice.

keyTeachings.title: Seven limbs
keyTeachings.text: It lists seven means: purification (shodhana through shatkarma), strengthening through asana, steadiness through mudra, calm through pratyahara, lightness through pranayama, perception of the self through dhyana, and detachment through samadhi.

keyTeachings.title: Kinds of meditation and samadhi
keyTeachings.text: Meditation is divided into gross, luminous and subtle forms, and samadhi is described through several methods, reflecting an inclusive, practice-oriented approach.

structure.label: Seven chapters (upadeshas)
structure.note: Roughly one for each of the seven limbs
